mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays depressed while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, daytime commuting and discretionary trip chaining weaken, so retail visits soften over the next four weeks relative to the prior four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell to -23.7 at t-0w while RESIDENTIAL stayed above baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the last 28 days when WORKPLACES is below baseline by more than 10 points and RESIDENTIAL is above baseline for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week drop in TRANSIT reduces spontaneous mall and street-front shopping trips within one week, because access friction immediately lowers retail visitation even if other categories are stable.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT dropped from 7.1 at t-1w to 1.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline within one week after a TRANSIT drop larger than 3 points, or rises instead, in repeated occurrences.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM is above baseline and still rising, households consolidate essential errands with nearby nonessential purchases, lifting retail traffic over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM above +8 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM reached 12.7 at t-1w and 10.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior four-week mean within two weeks after GROCERY_PHARM stays above +8 for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates renewed mobility restriction or office curtailment, and that combined shock suppresses retail spending over the next four weeks more than either series alone.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall below their prior-week values
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both weakened at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not underperform its last-28-day mean over the next four weeks when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES decline in the same week.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent PARKS weakness alongside elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility signals a stay-at-home leisure substitution, which reduces footfall in retail and recreation over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS stayed near -18 while RESIDENTIAL stayed above +5
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite PARKS remaining below baseline and RESIDENTIAL remaining above baseline for most of the period.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT rebounds back above baseline after a prior dip, delayed commuting and after-work shopping return quickly, producing a retail lift within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses from below 0 to above 0
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was positive in t-3w to t-1w before dropping to 1.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next two weeks after TRANSIT returns above baseline from a sub-baseline reading.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in GROCERY_PHARM together with flat-to-down WORKPLACES means routine errands are replacing discretionary outings, so retail-and-recreation mobility falls over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose while WORKPLACES turned sharply negative at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not underperform the last four weeks when GROCERY_PHARM is above baseline and WORKPLACES is below baseline for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a restriction-tightening regime, the combination of falling TRANSIT and falling PARKS is an early signal of reduced public circulation, and retail mobility drops within one week of that paired decline.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and PARKS both fall week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell to 1.6 at t-0w and PARKS stayed near -18
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within one week after both TRANSIT and PARKS weaken together under tightening restrictions.
